title: Emrys and the Parish
premise: Marguerite Dravenmoor, the meticulous archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, is hired to close the eleven-year-old disappearance of Verity Loxley, a parish benefactor whose diary was found in the locked crypt — with entries written after her vanishing date. As Marguerite decodes the diary's coded marginalia, they realize Verity staged her own disappearance to expose an inheritance fraud buried in the parish trust, and that someone has been maintaining her diary ever since to keep the secret alive. The killer is the cathedral's beloved verger, who has memorized every case file to erase evidence before investigators can read it. At the anniversary dinner honoring Verity's memory, Marguerite traps him by planting a forged diary page only he would recognize as false and rush to destroy, forcing his confession before the assembled parish.
about_author: Gideon Marchetti is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing centuries of church ledgers in rural England. Their fiction blends ecclesiastical history with slow-burn mysteries about the documents people leave behind.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Marguerite Dravenmoor's POV. A routine inventory of St. Aldhelm's crypt reveals Verity Loxley's diary wedged behind a saint's reliquary — sealed in a room locked since her disappearance. The final entry is dated three years after she vanished. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Terms of Closure
chapters.summary: Marguerite accepts the case from Verity's niece, Cordelia, who inherits nothing until the estate settles. Flashbacks establish Marguerite's rule: never take a case they can't close. Emotional beat: quiet confidence masking an old failure that haunts them.

chapters.title: Entries After Death
chapters.summary: Marguerite catalogs the diary chronologically and confirms the impossible: handwriting continues past the disappearance date, growing shakier. The verger, Mr. Pell, hovers during their research, quoting file details unprompted. Emotional beat: first brush of being watched.

chapters.title: The Benefactor's Ledger
chapters.summary: In the parish archive, Marguerite finds discrepancies in the Loxley Trust — donations rerouted through accounts signed by two trustees, one of whom died conveniently soon after. POV shifts briefly to Cordelia. Emotional beat: the dawning shape of an inheritance crime.

chapters.title: What the Sacristan Saw
chapters.summary: An elderly sacristan recalls Verity arguing with someone in the cloister the night she vanished, but the memory keeps shifting each time he tells it. Marguerite suspects coaching. Emotional beat: frustration at unreliable memory as both theme and obstacle.

chapters.title: Coded Marginalia
chapters.summary: Marguerite discovers the diary's margins carry a cipher keyed to hymn numbers, revealing Verity feared a trustee and hid evidence 'where the dead keep vigil.' Emotional beat: exhilaration of breakthrough shadowed by dread of what it implies.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Committee
chapters.summary: The parish prepares its annual dinner honoring Verity. Marguerite attends a planning meeting where Pell controls every record, every seating chart, every narrative. Emotional beat: recognition that the killer curates collective memory itself.

chapters.title: Where the Dead Keep Vigil
chapters.summary: Night search of the crypt yields a hollowed reliquary containing a second ledger — Verity's private accounting of the fraud, naming her partner in exposure: the then-young Mr. Pell. Emotional beat: vertigo; the helper may be the hunter.

chapters.title: A File Read Too Well
chapters.summary: Marguerite tests Pell by misquoting a case detail; he corrects them instantly, citing a page number no one should know. POV alternates with Pell's for the first time — his devotion to 'protecting' Verity's story. Emotional beat: cold confirmation.

chapters.title: Cordelia's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Cordelia admits she hired Marguerite hoping closure would unlock her inheritance — and that she once found a threatening note signed with Verity's initials, years after the disappearance. Emotional beat: complicity and fear entwined.

chapters.title: The Shifting Witness
chapters.summary: The sacristan recants entirely, then dies quietly in his sleep. Marguerite realizes memory itself is being murdered alongside witnesses. Emotional beat: grief and guilt for moving too slowly.

chapters.title: Pell's Sermon
chapters.summary: Pell delivers a memorial address so moving that the parish weeps; Marguerite watches a community choose comfort over truth. He warns Marguerite afterward, gently, that some cases are better left unclosed. Emotional beat: menace wrapped in tenderness.

chapters.title: The Forged Page
chapters.summary: Marguerite's plan forms: forge a diary page implicating an innocent trustee, seeded with deliberate errors only someone who memorized the true file would catch. They age paper, match ink, rehearse Verity's hand. Emotional beat: the archivist becoming a forger — justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: Bait in the Archive
chapters.summary: Marguerite plants the forged page in the public case file and tips off the diocese that new evidence exists. Surveillance of the crypt at night. Emotional beat: coiled patience, self-doubt about entrapment.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: Dinner preparations; Cordelia panics and nearly pulls out; Marguerite steadies her while noticing Pell has moved the reliquary — he knows something is wrong but not what. Emotional beat: the trap tightening around both hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: At the dinner, the chairman raises a glass to Verity. Marguerite publicly announces the discovery of 'new diary pages,' watching Pell's face across candlelight. Emotional beat: theatrical tension; the room becomes a stage.

chapters.title: The Error Only He Could See
chapters.summary: Pell slips away mid-dinner toward the crypt to destroy the forgery; Marguerite follows with Cordelia and the police inspector he's spent weeks misleading. They catch him burning the page — and confessing aloud to the empty saints. Emotional beat: triumph laced with pity.

chapters.title: Confession in the Crypt
chapters.summary: Pell explains: he loved Verity, helped her hide the ledger, then killed her when she wavered, and kept the diary alive to preserve the woman rather than the truth. Emotional beat: devastating humanity inside monstrosity.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: The inspector must decide whether Marguerite's forgery taints the case; the confession, witnessed, holds. Marguerite confronts the cost of their methods against their old unresolved failure. Emotional beat: reckoning with means and ends.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: The trust is unwound; Cordelia receives her inheritance and donates much of it to restoring the crypt archive. The sacristan's name is added to the memorial roll. Emotional beat: bittersweet restitution.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Marguerite writes the diary's true final entry in Verity's voice, closing the account honestly, and locks the crypt — this time with the truth inside. Emotional beat: peace earned through precision.

chapters.title: A Case Closed
chapters.summary: Epilogue. A new client arrives with an impossible document; Marguerite, changed, weighs whether to take it. Final image: the cathedral bells ringing over a parish that remembers differently now. Emotional beat: continuity, vigilance, quiet hope.
